title: Cannabis Popsicles: Easy Infused THC Ice Pops
metaDescription: Make fruity or creamy adults-only cannabis popsicles with infused simple syrup, mixed for an even dose in every pop and stored safely away from kids.
excerpt: Adults-only ice pops sweetened with infused simple syrup, mixed so every pop carries a similar dose, and stored where kids can't mistake them for theirs.
keyTakeaways: Divide the mg in your infused syrup by the number of molds, and stir well between pours.
Pour with headroom, freeze until slushy, add the sticks, then freeze solid.
Keep the look plain and grown-up: no novelty molds or cartoon colors.
Store the pops in a sealed, labeled box on a high freezer shelf, never next to kids' frozen desserts.
body:
Cannabis popsicles are a grown-up frozen dessert for hot Michigan days: fruit juice or puree sweetened with infused simple syrup and frozen in molds. What matters most is an even dose in every pop and a freezer plan that keeps them away from kids.

## Dosing: divide by the molds

Divide the THC in the infused syrup you use by the number of pops. Say your [infused simple syrup](/blog/infused-simple-syrup/) works out to about 5 mg per teaspoon. For 10 pops at 2.5 mg each, you'd stir in 5 teaspoons (25 mg) and sweeten the rest of the way with plain syrup. A pop can take 2 hours to make itself felt, and the effects can last 4 to 12, so have one and wait. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) covers starting amounts.

## What you need

Fruit juice or puree (or puree with a splash of cream or coconut milk), your measured infused syrup and plain syrup to taste; fresh fruit, mint or basil are optional. Flower for a batch of syrup can be ordered for pickup from [your nearest High Society store's menu](/shop/).

## How to make cannabis popsicles

Whisk the base and syrups for a full 30 seconds, since infusions can settle in a water-based mix, and stir again between pours. Leave 1/4 inch of headroom, freeze until slushy, add the sticks and freeze solid. Running warm water over the molds releases the pops.

## Flavor ideas

- Orange and mango
- Strawberry lemonade, or our [frozen strawberry canna-nade](/blog/frozen-strawberry-canna-nade/)
- Coconut and lime
- Mixed berries with mint or basil

Keep the look plain and grown-up. As of October 2026, Michigan's rules for licensed edibles bar shapes, cartoons and packaging that appeal to minors. Those rules cover licensed products, not your kitchen, but the reasoning holds: skip novelty molds and cartoon colors.

## Storage and labeling

Frozen pops look like kids' food. A 2023 study of U.S. poison center data counted 3,054 cases of children younger than 6 eating cannabis edibles in 2021, against 207 in 2017, and nearly every case happened in a home.

- Store the pops in a sealed, opaque container labeled "THC, adults only," with the mg per pop and the date.
- Keep it high in the freezer, never with kids' frozen desserts.
- Serve them only to adults 21 and older who've been told they're infused, never at gatherings with kids.

If a child eats one, call Poison Control right away at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 in an emergency; if a pet does, call your veterinarian or an animal poison control center. Our guide to [cannabis and parenting](/blog/cannabis-and-parenting/) has more storage ideas.

faq.q: How do I make sure each popsicle has the same dose?
faq.a: Mix thoroughly and measure. Whisk the infused syrup into the whole batch before pouring, stir again between molds and fill every mold to the same line. Then divide the total mg by the number of pops, and use a measuring cup if your molds vary in size.

faq.q: How long do cannabis popsicles take to kick in?
faq.a: Health Canada's range is half an hour to 2 hours, with the full effect as late as 4 hours in, and effects can last 4 to 12 hours. A cold pop goes down fast, so it's easy to reach for a second too soon. Have one, give it at least 2 hours and stay off the road.

faq.q: Can I use a tincture instead of syrup?
faq.a: Yes. Stir the measured tincture into the base with your regular sweetener and whisk well, since tinctures can separate in a water-based mix. Use the mg per mL on the label to work out the total, then divide by the number of pops. Glycerin tinctures taste sweet; alcohol ones taste sharper.

sources.label: Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency: Marihuana Rules, R 420.1 to R 420.1004 (PDF)
Tweet M.S. et al., Pediatric Edible Cannabis Exposures and Acute Toxicity: 2017-2021, Pediatrics (2023)
Health Canada: Cannabis, lower your risks
Public Health Agency of Canada: Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health statement on cannabis extracts, edibles and topicals (2020)
America's Poison Centers: Frequently asked questions (pet poisonings)

ingredients: 3 cups fruit juice or puree (or 2 1/2 cups puree plus 1/2 cup cream or coconut milk)
Infused simple syrup, measured for your dose (see the note)
Plain simple syrup or sugar, to taste
Optional: 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, chopped fresh fruit, a few mint or basil leaves
steps: Taste the base and sweeten it with plain syrup or sugar first.
Whisk in the measured infused syrup for a full 30 seconds.
Pour into 10 molds, leaving about 1/4 inch of headroom, and stir the base again between pours.
Freeze for 1 to 2 hours, until slushy, then insert the sticks.
Freeze until solid, at least 4 more hours or overnight.
Run warm water over the outside of the molds for 10 to 20 seconds to release the pops.
Store the pops in a sealed, labeled freezer container on a high shelf.
recipe.dosingNote: Estimate only: say your infused syrup works out to about 5 mg per teaspoon. Five teaspoons carry about 25 mg, or 2.5 mg per pop across 10 pops. A syrup's true strength depends on what went into it and on what decarbing and infusing cost along the way. One pop is a full first serving; wait at least 2 hours before another. The freezer box needs a clear label and a high shelf, away from kids and pets.

claims.claim: Example: syrup at about 5 mg per teaspoon; 5 tsp = 25 mg = 2.5 mg per pop across 10 pops
claims.source: Arithmetic; 5 mg/tsp is a stated example.

claims.claim: 2.5 mg per pop as a full first serving
claims.source: CCMOH statement (Jan. 6, 2020): 'Start with small amounts - 2.5 mg of THC or less'; Health Canada, Cannabis: lower your risks: 'Look for products that contain 2.5 mg of THC or less'. Both opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: A pop can take 2 hours to be felt; effects can last 4 to 12 hours
claims.source: CCMOH 2020: 'up to 2 hours to feel the effects'; 'last 4 to 12 hours'.

claims.claim: FAQ: half an hour to 2 hours 'for most people', full effect as late as 4 hours
claims.fix: The source gives the range without 'for most people'; now attributed: 'Health Canada's range is half an hour to 2 hours'.
claims.source: Health Canada: 'Effects felt within 30 minutes to 2 hours'; 'It can take up to 4 hours to feel the full effects'.

claims.claim: Give it 2 hours / wait 2 hours before another (FAQ, dosing note)
claims.fix: Now 'at least 2 hours' in both places.
claims.source: Health Canada: full effects can take up to 4 hours.

claims.claim: Infusions can settle in a water-based mix; whisk 30 seconds and stir between pours
claims.source: PubChem CID 16078 (Solubility): THC 'Essentially insoluble in water'.

claims.claim: Leave 1/4 inch of headroom; freeze until slushy, add sticks, freeze solid; warm water for 10-20 seconds releases the pops
claims.source: Method; water expands as it freezes.

claims.claim: Yield: 10 pops in 3-ounce molds from 3 cups of base plus syrups
claims.source: Arithmetic: 24 fl oz of base plus syrups is about 26-27 oz, which fills ten 3-oz molds with headroom.

claims.claim: As of October 2026, Michigan's rules for licensed edibles bar shapes, cartoons and packaging that appeal to minors; the rules cover licensed products, not home kitchens
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-edibles (R 420.403(9), CRA Marihuana Rules PDF): no shapes, labels, cartoons, toys or packaging that appeal to minors. The rules bind licensees.

claims.claim: 2023 study of US poison center data: 3,054 cases of children under 6 eating cannabis edibles in 2021 vs 207 in 2017; nearly every case in a home
claims.source: Tweet, Nemanich & Wahl, Pediatrics 2023 (PMID 36594224; abstract via NCBI E-utilities 2026-10-24): National Poison Data System, children <6; '207 reported cases' in 2017, '3054 cases' in 2021; '97.7% occurred in a residential setting'. Dated as 2017-2021 data in the text.

claims.claim: Sealed, opaque, labeled container high in the freezer, never with kids' desserts; serve only to informed adults 21+, never at gatherings with kids
If a child or pet gets into one, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.fix: The number is right for people; America's Poison Centers says member centers need not take pet calls and points to a veterinarian or animal poison center. Now: child, call 1-800-222-1222 or 911 in an emergency; pet, call a veterinarian or an animal poison control center. Source added.
claims.source: CDC Cannabis FAQ (Jan. 31, 2025): 'call a poison control center at ... 1-800-222-1222', 'In case of emergency, call 9-1-1'; America's Poison Centers FAQ, https://www.poisonhelp.org/faq. Both opened 2026-10-24.

claims.claim: FAQ: a tincture can replace syrup; tinctures can separate in water; glycerin tinctures taste sweet, alcohol ones sharper
High Society: flower for a batch of syrup can be ordered for pickup from your nearest store's menu
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering; no product or stock claimed.

claims.claim: Sources resolve and support the text
claims.source: Tweet 2023 (E-utilities), Health Canada, CCMOH and CDC opened 2026-10-24; the CRA Marihuana Rules PDF is the law-facts source for mi-edibles (michigan.gov refuses automated fetches; verified there).

review.factCheckNotes: Fact-check 2026-10-24: 15 claims checked, 3 fixed ('for most people', wait time, pet poisoning). Added the America's Poison Centers FAQ as a source.
review.writerNotes: Riskiest topic in the batch for appeal to minors (R 420.507 and R 420.403): no cartoonish or kid-style presentation, no mixed-age serving, storage gets as much space as flavor. The CRA edible rules are described as covering licensed products, with the home advice framed as reasoning, not law.
